item.title: Apple Taps American Airlines Veteran as Government Affairs Head
item.description: Apple Inc. hired Nate Gatten as its new head of government affairs, tapping a longtime American Airlines Group Inc. executive with Republican ties to handle a delicate role at the company.

item.title: Uber Working on Offering ‘Tween’ Rides Option for Kids 10 to 12
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. is working on offering rides to kids between the ages of 10 and 12, marking a possible expansion into its youngest demographic yet.

item.title: DeepSeek Publicizes Efforts to Challenge Anthropic’s Claude Code
item.description: DeepSeek has set up an official social media account and posted job listings for a new team focused on helping develop artificial intelligence agents that can take on services like Anthropic PBC’s popular Claude Code.

item.title: UniCredit’s Commerzbank Bid Nears ECB Approval, Reuters Reports
item.description: The European Central Bank is leaning toward ​approving UniCredit SpA’s takeover of Germany’s Commerzbank AG, Reuters reported, citing an internal document presented last month to the central bank’s Supervisory Board.

item.title: UK Plans Safeguards to Stop Terrorists Using AI For Bioweapons
item.description: The UK government is planning to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in gene synthesis as officials become increasingly concerned that a lack of global guardrails could make it easier to use the technology to create biological weapons.

item.title: Air Baltic Bonds Slump After Airline’s Debt-for-Equity Swap Plan
item.description: Bonds issued by Air Baltic Corp slumped further into deeply distressed levels after the ailing Latvian airline announced plans to swap much of its debt for equity as part of a restructuring plan.

item.title: US Launches Effort to Speed Trade in AI Goods Between Allies
item.description: The Trump administration announced a new program aimed at accelerating shipments between the US and its closest trading partners of goods considered critical to developing artificial intelligence.

item.title: Formlabs Partners With Former Apple Hardware Chief Dan Riccio
item.description: Formlabs, a maker of 3D printers, shook up its board as former Apple Inc. hardware chief Dan Riccio took a stake in the company and became a strategic adviser.

item.title: German Firms See Expanding AI Use Crimping Wages, Survey Shows
item.description: German companies deploying artificial intelligence are expecting its growing use to depress wages over the next five years, especially for junior workers.

item.title: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Tries to Reinvent the Camera Flash
item.description: With rivals pushing fresher designs, Google’s latest models risk getting overlooked despite subtle tweaks.

item.title: Google to Track Insulin Trends With New Wearables Feature on Watch 5, Fitbit Air
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google is bringing a new set of health features to its wearables, including one that tracks insulin resistance over time, marking a first for consumer tech companies that are working to eventually crack comprehensive blood-sugar monitoring.

item.title: Milei Eases Cash Crunch to Reignite Economic Growth in Argentina
item.description: President Javier Milei’s administration is starting to shift its focus from solely crushing inflation to a more balanced act as growth, jobs and his approval ratings struggle to pick up.

item.title: JPMorgan Sees Fed on Hold as ‘Teflon Inflation’ Eases Concerns
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management’s chief global strategist said the Federal Reserve should keep interest rates unchanged and predicted that inflation will gradually come down as evidence mounts that a sustained wage-price spiral won’t take root.

item.title: JPMorgan, Goldman, Invesco Test Blockchain Across Wall Street
item.description: For four hours in July, some of the biggest players in finance put Wall Street’s long-running blockchain experiment to work across an ordinary trading day.

item.title: A Favorite Carry Trade Gets a Dose of Brazil Election Jitters
item.description: Election worries are starting to seep into Brazilian markets, prompting some investors to pare exposure to one of this year’s most rewarding carry trades as they brace for a bumpier ride into the October presidential vote.

item.title: Yardeni Raises S&P 500 View to 8,400 on ‘Fabulous Earnings’
item.description: Ed Yardeni is raising his view for the S&P 500 Index to a level that tops his own Street-high target for the gauge after “fabulous earnings momentum.”

item.title: Russia Daily Oil Output Almost Million Barrels Below OPEC+ Quota
item.description: Russia’s crude-only production lagged behind its OPEC+ quota by almost a million barrels a day in July as Ukraine attacked the nation’s oil infrastructure almost daily.

item.title: Lightspeed Seeks $600 Million for Anthropic, OpenAI Wagers
item.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is seeking about $600 million in a secondary process to extend its ownership of OpenAI and four other assets, as well as a new commitment to Anthropic PBC, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US CPI Report July 2026: Key Takeaways on Inflation, Consumer Price Index
item.description: Here are the key takeaways from the US consumer price index report for July, released Wednesday:

item.title: Mark Bezos’ Fund Faces Fight to Recoup Losses From Fence Startup
item.description: A venture capital firm co-founded by Jeff Bezos’ younger brother Mark sank $11.7 million into a startup that fashioned itself as an Uber of fence installation. Now it’s suing the startup’s founder after the company’s collapse amid allegations of fraud and mismanagement.

item.title: Hungary to Raise Danube Riverbed to Help Cool Its Nuclear Plant
item.description: Hungary is starting work on a riverbed structure to raise the water level of the Danube at the central city of Paks, in order to support the operation of the country’s sole nuclear facility, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said.

item.title: New York City’s Five Pensions Gain 13% on Surging US Stocks
item.description: New York City’s five pensions beat their investment target over the past fiscal year, propelled by a record-breaking US stock market.

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Startup CodeRabbit Valued at $1.5 Billion in Round
item.description: CodeRabbit Inc., an artificial intelligence-powered code review service, has raised $143 million in a new funding round, tapping into demand for tools to spot flaws in AI-generated software programming.

item.title: Bond Traders Keep Cointoss Wager on September Fed Hike Post-CPI
item.description: Traders held on to their hedges that Federal Reserve officials could raise interest rates at their next meeting in September, pricing in a roughly 50% chance of a move after a tame reading of US inflation.

item.title: Whoop Plans to Double Size of Boston Headquarters Ahead of IPO
item.description: Whoop Inc., the maker of popular screenless fitness trackers, plans to roughly double the size of its Boston headquarters, boosting a city struggling to grab a bigger piece of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Real Estate Fund Set to Lose Boston Life Science Investment
item.description: A small US commercial real estate fund run by Deutsche Finance Group, the asset manager tied to many of the soured deals at German pension fund BVK, plans to file for insolvency after its investment in a Boston life sciences complex soured.

item.title: Hormuz Closure Helps Emerging-Market Company Bonds Beat US Peers
item.description: The average borrowing cost of emerging-market companies has fallen to the lowest level since January relative to US corporates as global bond investors’ diversification into higher-yielding assets drives an outperformance.

item.title: US Core Inflation Comes in Subdued, Easing Pressure on Fed
item.description: Underlying US inflation was subdued in July, likely easing pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: Potential ‘Peak Earnings’ Set the Stage for Disappointing Stocks
item.description: The latest reason to worry about the stock market is quite the doozy: Earnings growth has been too strong.

item.title: Vestas CEO Says EU Prevents Mergers Needed to Compete Globally
item.description: Europe’s wind turbine makers would be better able to compete globally if regulators in Brussels allowed more consolidation, according to the chief executive officer of Vestas Wind Systems A/S.
